source_text: Ἀλλὰ τοῦτό ἐστιν ἑαυτὸν σοφώτερον ποιοῦντος τῶν λογίων τοῦ Πνεύματος, καὶ ἐν προσποιήσει ἐξηγήσεως τὰ ἑαυτοῦ παρεισάγοντος. Νοείσθω τοίνυν ὡς γέγραπται. 9.2 Ἐξαγαγέτω ἡ γῆ ψυχὴν ζῶσαν κτηνῶν καὶ θηρίων καὶ ἑρπετῶν. Νόησον ῥῆμα Θεοῦ διὰ τῆς κτίσεως τρέχον, καὶ τότε ἀρξάμενον, καὶ μέχρι νῦν ἐνεργοῦν, καὶ εἰς τέλος δεξιὸν, ἕως ἂν ὁ κόσμος συμπληρωθῇ. Ὡς γὰρ ἡ σφαῖρα, ἐπειδὰν ὑπό τινος ἀπωσθῇ, εἶτα πρανοῦς τινος λάβηται, ὑπό τε τῆς οἰκείας κατασκευῆς καὶ τῆς ἐπιτηδειότητος τοῦ χωρίου φέρεται πρὸς τὸ κάταντες, οὐ πρότερον ἱσταμένη πρὶν ἄν τι τῶν ἰσοπέδων αὐτὴν ὑποδέξηται· οὕτως ἡ φύσις τῶν ὄντων ἑνὶ προστάγματι κινηθεῖσα, τὴν ἐν τῇ γενέσει καὶ φθορᾷ κτίσιν ὁμαλῶς διεξέρχεται, τὰς τῶν γενῶν ἀκολουθίας δι' ὁμοιότητος ἀποσώζουσα, ἕως ἂν πρὸς αὐτὸ καταντήσῃ τὸ τέλος. Ἵππον μὲν γὰρ ἵππου ποιεῖται διάδοχον, καὶ λέοντα λέοντος, καὶ ἀετὸν ἀετοῦ· καὶ ἕκαστον τῶν ζῴων ταῖς ἐφεξῆς διαδοχαῖς συντηρούμενον μέχρι τῆς συντελείας τοῦ παντὸς παραπέμπει. Οὐδεὶς χρόνος διεφθαρμένα ἢ ἐξίτηλα ποιεῖ τῶν ζῴων τὰ ἰδιώματα, ἀλλ' ὥσπερ ἄρτι καθισταμένη ἡ φύσις ἀεὶ νεαρὰ τῷ χρόνῳ συμπαρατρέχει. Ἐξαγαγέτω ἡ γῆ ψυχὴν ζῶσαν. Τοῦτο ἐναπέμεινε τῇ γῇ τὸ πρόσταγμα, καὶ οὐ παύεται ἐξυπηρετουμένη τῷ κτίσαντι. Τὰ μὲν γὰρ ἐκ τῆς διαδοχῆς τῶν προϋπαρχόντων παράγεται· τὰ δὲ ἔτι καὶ νῦν ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς γῆς ζῳογονούμενα δείκνυται. Οὐ γὰρ μόνον τέττιγας ἐν ἐπομβρίαις ἀνίησιν, οὐδὲ ἄλλα μυρία γένη τῶν ἐμφερομένων τῷ ἀέρι πτηνῶν, ὧν ἀκατωνόμαστά ἐστι τὰ πλεῖστα διὰ λεπτότητα, ἀλλ' ἤδη καὶ μῦς καὶ βατράχους ἐξ αὐτῆς ἀναδίδωσιν. Ὅπου γε περὶ Θήβας τὰς Αἰγυπτίας ἐπειδὰν ὕσῃ λάβρως ἐν καύμασιν, εὐθὺς ἀρουραίων μυῶν ἡ χώρα καταπληροῦται. Τὰς δὲ ἐγχέλεις οὐδὲ ἄλλως ὁρῶμεν ἢ ἐκ τῆς ἰλύος συνισταμένας· ὧν οὔτε ὠὸν οὔτε τις ἄλλος τρόπος τὴν διαδοχὴν συνίστησιν, ἀλλ' ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐστιν αὐτοῖς ἡ γένεσις. Ἐξαγαγέτω ἡ γῆ ψυχήν. Τὰ κτήνη γήϊνα καὶ πρὸς γῆν νενευκότα, ἀλλὰ τὸ οὐράνιον φυτὸν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὅσον τῷ σχήματι τῆς σωματικῆς διαπλάσεως, τοσοῦτον καὶ τῷ ἀξιώματι τῆς ψυχῆς διενήνοχε. Τῶν τετραπόδων τὸ σχῆμα ποταπόν; Ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ γῆν προσνένευκεν, ἐπὶ γαστέρα βλέπει, καὶ τὸ ταύτης ἡδὺ ἐκ παντὸς τρόπου διώκει. Ἡ σὴ κεφαλὴ πρὸς οὐρανὸν διανέστηκεν· οἱ ὀφθαλμοί σου τὰ ἄνω βλέπουσιν, ὡς ἐάν ποτε καὶ σὺ τοῖς πάθεσι τῆς σαρκὸς ἑαυτὸν ἀτιμάσῃς, γαστρὶ δουλεύων καὶ τοῖς ὑπὸ γαστέρα, παρασυνεβλήθης τοῖς κτήνεσι τοῖς ἀνοήτοις, καὶ ὡμοιώθης αὐτοῖς. Ἄλλη σοι μέριμνα πρέπουσα, τὰ ἄνω ζητεῖν, οὗ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν, ὑπὲρ τὰ γήϊνα εἶναι τῇ διανοίᾳ. Ὡς διεσχηματίσθης, οὕτω διάθου σεαυτοῦ καὶ τὸν βίον. Τὸ πολίτευμα ἔχε ἐν οὐρανοῖς. Ἀληθινή σου πατρὶς ἡ ἄνω Ἱερουσαλὴμ, πολῖται καὶ συμφυλέται οἱ πρωτότοκοι, οἱ ἀπογεγραμμένοι ἐν οὐρανοῖς. 9.3 Ἐξαγαγέτω ἡ γῆ ψυχὴν ζῶσαν. Οὐ τοίνυν ἐναποκειμένη τῇ γῇ ἡ ψυχὴ τῶν ἀλόγων ἐξεφάνη, ἀλλ' ὁμοῦ τῷ προστάγματι συνυπέστη. Μία δὲ ψυχὴ τῶν ἀλόγων. Ἓν γὰρ αὐτὴν τὸ χαρακτηρίζον ἐστὶν, ἡ ἀλογία.
thought_title: The earth's command to bring forth living creatures
orientation: Basil is expounding Genesis 1:24, where God commands the earth to bring forth living creatures, and is contrasting the earth-bound posture of animals with the heavenward posture of man.
pass_a_gloss: But this is the act of one making himself wiser than the oracles of the Spirit, and under pretense of interpretation introducing his own ideas. Let it be understood therefore as it is written. Let the earth bring forth a living creature of cattle and wild beasts and creeping things. Understand the word of God running through creation, both then beginning, and until now working, and toward a good end, until the world is completed. For as a sphere, whenever it is pushed by someone, then takes hold of some slope, by its own construction and the suitability of the place is carried toward the downward slope, not stopping before some level ground receives it; so the nature of existing things, moved by one command, passes through the creation in generation and corruption evenly, preserving the successions of the kinds through similarity, until it arrives at the end itself. For it makes a horse the successor of a horse, and a lion of a lion, and an eagle of an eagle; and each of the animals, preserved by the successive successions, it sends forward until the completion of the whole. No time makes the characteristics of the animals corrupted or faded, but as if just now established, the nature always runs along fresh with time. Let the earth bring forth a living creature. This command remained in the earth, and it does not cease serving the Creator. For some things are produced from the succession of pre-existing things; but others even now are shown being generated alive from the earth itself. For not only does it send up cicadas in heavy rains, nor other countless kinds of winged things borne in the air, of which most are unnamed because of smallness, but already it also sends up mice and frogs from itself. Where indeed around Thebes in Egypt, whenever it rains violently in the heat, immediately the country is filled with field mice. And eels we see in no other way than being formed from the mud; of which neither egg nor any other manner establishes the succession, but from the earth is their origin. Let the earth bring forth a living creature. The cattle are earthy and bent toward the earth, but the heavenly plant, man, as much in the form of his bodily shaping, so much also in the dignity of his soul has differed. What is the form of the quadrupeds? Their head is bent down to the earth, looks toward the belly, and pursues its pleasure in every way. Your head stands up toward heaven; your eyes look at the things above, so that if ever you also dishonor yourself with the passions of the flesh, serving the belly and the things under the belly, you have been compared to the senseless cattle, and you have become like them. Another care befits you, to seek the things above, where Christ is, to be above the earthly things in your mind. As you have been shaped, so also arrange your life. Have your citizenship in the heavens. Your true fatherland is the Jerusalem above, citizens and fellow-tribesmen the firstborn, the ones enrolled in the heavens. Let the earth bring forth a living creature. Not therefore was the soul of the irrational animals lying stored up in the earth and appeared, but together with the command it came into existence. And one is the soul of the irrational animals. For one thing characterizes it, the irrationality.

choices.why: The glossary mandates this rendering for the phrase, used of animals as distinct from plants.
The imperative force of the divine command is preserved in the literal rendering.
Basil's metaphor for man as a plant whose nature is oriented toward heaven; literal rendering keeps the image.
The passive aorist indicates a completed action of being likened; the literal rendering preserves the passive voice.
The noun denotes one's commonwealth or civic status; the literal rendering fits Basil's exhortation to heavenly citizenship.

pass_b_english: But this is what someone does when he makes himself wiser than the oracles of the Spirit, and under the pretense of interpretation smuggles in his own ideas. Let it be understood, then, as it is written.

“Let the earth bring forth the living creature of cattle and wild beasts and creeping things” (Genesis 1:24). Consider the word of God running through creation, beginning then and still at work now, and pressing on to a prosperous end until the world is completed. For just as a ball, when someone pushes it and it finds a slope, is carried downhill by its own construction and the suitability of the ground, and does not stop until something level receives it, so the nature of existing things, set in motion by a single command, passes evenly through the creation that is subject to birth and decay, preserving the successions of kinds through likeness, until it arrives at the end itself. For it makes a horse the successor of a horse, and a lion of a lion, and an eagle of an eagle, and it hands on each of the animals, preserved through successive generations, until the completion of all things. No time corrupts or makes obsolete the distinctive traits of animals, but their nature, as if just now established, always fresh, runs along with time.

“Let the earth bring forth the living creature.” This command remained in the earth, and it does not cease serving the Creator. For some creatures are brought forth from the succession of those that existed before, but others are shown even now to be generated alive from the earth itself. For not only does it send up cicadas in rainy seasons, and countless other kinds of winged creatures borne in the air, most of which are nameless because of their smallness, but it already also produces mice and frogs from itself. Indeed, around Thebes in Egypt, whenever it rains heavily in the heat, the country is immediately filled with field mice. And we see that eels are formed in no other way than from the mud; neither an egg nor any other method establishes their succession, but their origin is from the earth.

“Let the earth bring forth the living creature.” The cattle are earthy and bent toward the ground, but man, the heavenly plant, differs as much in the dignity of his soul as in the shape of his bodily form. What is the shape of the four-footed animals? Their head is bent down toward the earth, it looks toward the belly, and it pursues the belly's pleasure in every way. Your head stands upright toward heaven; your eyes look upward. So if you ever dishonor yourself with the passions of the flesh, serving the belly and the parts beneath it, you have been grouped with the senseless cattle and have become like them. A different concern befits you: to seek the things above, where Christ is (Colossians 3:1-2), and to be above earthly things in your mind. As you have been shaped, so order your life as well. Have your citizenship in heaven (Philippians 3:20). Your true homeland is the Jerusalem above, and your fellow citizens and kin are the firstborn, enrolled in heaven (Hebrews 12:22-23).

“Let the earth bring forth the living creature.” The soul of the irrational animals, then, was not stored up in the earth and then revealed, but came into existence together with the command. And the soul of the irrational animals is one. For the one thing that characterizes it is irrationality.

problems.quote: you have been compared to the senseless cattle and have become like them
problems.source_quote: παρασυνεβλήθης τοῖς κτήνεσι τοῖς ἀνοήτοις, καὶ ὡμοιώθης αὐτοῖς
problems.why: Two distinct verbs: 'παρασυνεβλήθης' (you were grouped alongside) and 'ὡμοιώθης' (you were made like); English merges them.
problems.fix: you were grouped with the senseless cattle and were made like them

problems.quote: pressing on to its proper end
problems.why: 'δεξιὸν' means 'right, prosperous, favorable' not 'proper'; 'pressing on to its proper end' loses the sense of success/blessing.
problems.fix: and pressing on to a prosperous end
problems.ruling: δεξιὸν means 'right/favorable', not 'proper'; 'proper end' loses the sense of a blessed/fitting end.

problems.quote: as if just now established, runs alongside time always fresh
problems.source_quote: ὥσπερ ἄρτι καθισταμένη ἡ φύσις ἀεὶ νεαρὰ τῷ χρόνῳ συμπαρατρέχει
problems.why: 'συμπαρατρέχει' means 'runs along together with', but 'νεαρὰ' modifies 'φύσις' (nature always fresh), not 'runs alongside time always fresh'.
problems.fix: nature, as if just now established, always fresh, runs along with time
problems.ruling: ἀεὶ νεαρὰ modifies ἡ φύσις ('nature always fresh'), not the verb; English 'runs alongside time always fresh' misattaches the adjective.

edits.old: you have been compared to the senseless cattle and have become like them
edits.new: you have been grouped with the senseless cattle and have become like them

edits.old: pressing on to its proper end
edits.new: pressing on to a prosperous end

edits.old: their nature, as if just now established, runs alongside time always fresh
edits.new: their nature, as if just now established, always fresh, runs along with time

fixed: παρασυνεβλήθης and ὡμοιώθης are two distinct verbs; English merged them. Changed to 'grouped with' and 'have become like'.
δεξιὸν means 'right, prosperous, favorable', not 'proper'. Changed 'proper end' to 'prosperous end'.
νεαρὰ modifies φύσις, not the running. Changed to 'always fresh, runs along with time'.

last_rejected.quote: pressing on to a prosperous end
last_rejected.why: δεξιὸν means 'right/favorable' but 'prosperous' overstates; 'right end' or 'fitting end' better captures the sense of proper completion.
last_rejected.fix: pressing on to a rightful end
last_rejected.ruling: δεξιὸν = 'right/favorable'; 'prosperous end' is within normal range, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: preserving the successions of kinds through likeness
last_rejected.source_quote: τὰς τῶν γενῶν ἀκολουθίας δι' ὁμοιότητος ἀποσώζουσα
last_rejected.why: ἀποσώζουσα means 'preserving/saving' but 'successions' for ἀκολουθίας is weak; 'sequences' or 'continuities' better, and 'through likeness' obscures that similarity is the means of preservation.
last_rejected.fix: preserving the continuities of kinds through similarity
last_rejected.ruling: ἀκολουθίας = 'successions'; 'preserving through likeness' captures ἀποσώζουσα δι' ὁμοιότητος adequately.

last_rejected.quote: it hands on each of the animals, preserved through successive generations
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ἕκαστον τῶν ζῴων ταῖς ἐφεξῆς διαδοχαῖς συντηρούμενον μέχρι τῆς συντελείας τοῦ παντὸς παραπέμπει
last_rejected.why: παραπέμπει means 'sends on/transmits,' not 'hands on'; συντηρούμενον is 'preserved' but the syntax makes 'each animal, being preserved through successive replacements, it transmits onward'—the subject is nature, not the animal preserving itself.
last_rejected.fix: and each of the animals, preserved through successive replacements, it transmits until the completion of all things
last_rejected.ruling: παραπέμπει = 'sends on/hands on'; rendering within normal range, no meaning changed.

last_rejected.quote: generated alive from the earth itself
last_rejected.why: ζῳογονούμενα means 'given life/made alive,' not 'generated alive'; the point is vivification, not manner of generation.
last_rejected.fix: given life from the earth itself
last_rejected.ruling: ζῳογονούμενα = 'made alive/given life'; 'generated alive' conveys this adequately.

last_rejected.quote: winged creatures borne in the air
last_rejected.why: ἐμφερομένων means 'carried along/moving in,' but 'borne' suggests passive support; these are creatures that move through air, not merely borne by it.
last_rejected.fix: winged creatures moving through the air
last_rejected.ruling: ἐμφερομένων = 'carried/borne'; 'borne in the air' is within normal range for πτηνῶν.

last_rejected.quote: but it already also produces mice and frogs from itself
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλ' ἤδη καὶ μῦς καὶ βατράχους ἐξ αὐτῆς ἀναδίδωσιν
last_rejected.why: ἀναδίδωσιν means 'gives up/emits/sends up,' not 'produces'; 'already' for ἤδη is fine but 'produces' loses the sense of the earth yielding up what was in it.
last_rejected.fix: but it also gives up mice and frogs from itself
last_rejected.ruling: ἀναδίδωσιν = 'gives up/sends up/produces'; 'produces' is within normal range.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλὰ τὸ οὐράνιον φυτὸν ὁ ἄνθρωπος
last_rejected.why: ὁ ἄνθρωπος is the subject, not in apposition; 'but man is the heavenly plant' or 'but as for man, he is the heavenly plant'—the English makes 'the heavenly plant' seem like a title rather than a predicate.
last_rejected.fix: but man is the heavenly plant
last_rejected.ruling: Apposition vs predicate is a stylistic preference; 'man, the heavenly plant' conveys the meaning.

last_rejected.quote: Your head stands upright toward heaven
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἡ σὴ κεφαλὴ πρὸς οὐρανὸν διανέστηκεν
last_rejected.why: διανέστηκεν is perfect tense, 'has been raised up/stands raised,' emphasizing the completed state; 'stands upright' loses the perfect aspect and the sense of being raised up.
last_rejected.fix: Your head has been raised up toward heaven
last_rejected.ruling: διανέστηκεν = 'stands apart/upright'; 'stands upright toward heaven' captures meaning adequately.

last_rejected.quote: A different concern befits you: to seek the things above, where Christ is
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἄλλη σοι μέριμνα πρέπουσα, τὰ ἄνω ζητεῖν, οὗ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν
last_rejected.why: The Greek has two separate items: 'another concern befits you: to seek the things above, where Christ is, [and] to be above earthly things in mind'; English merges them awkwardly with 'and to be above' becoming subordinate.
last_rejected.fix: A different concern befits you: to seek the things above, where Christ is, and to be above earthly things in mind
last_rejected.ruling: English has 'to seek...where Christ is, and to be above earthly things'; both items present, not merged.
